records.title: Spec-Centered Progressive Disclosure
records.articleSummary: Progressive disclosure keeps ordinary entry small: read the agent contract, follow the Runbook and Lexicon routes, then load the assigned capability and its relevant source. A Spec carries the assignment and its proof; the hot Taskboard derives an operational view. Reading an entire historical catalog is not a prerequisite for doing one bounded piece of work.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Held-Out Path-Safety Evaluation
records.articleSummary: The held-out task adds a security-oriented path-handling domain beside the development task. Its grader checks the produced repository and transcript without using the harness condition as an input to the grade. Keeping the held-out seam separate reduces the temptation to optimize only for familiar development fixtures.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Dependency-Safe Direct Claiming
records.articleSummary: Direct claiming must enforce the same dependencies as selection. An agent may already know its assigned Spec and skip a general selector; that shortcut must not let it claim a ready Task whose prerequisite is unfinished.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Consistent Bootstrap Ownership Guidance
records.articleSummary: A new project inherits its operating model through public setup instructions and the copy-ready Genesis and Adoption procedures. If those entry points use obsolete ownership language, they can recreate the very duplication that the harness removed internally.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Evidence-Gated Harness Feedback
records.articleSummary: The feedback loop separates candidate construction from an independent integration decision. Discovery reads the declared feedback lane first, then supported legacy feedback filenames. It excludes noncanonical project copies, normalizes origins, ranks candidates by impact and recurrence, and selects no new candidate while a pending fingerprint already exists.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Import-Safe Feedback Helper Entry
records.articleSummary: A JavaScript file can be both a command-line program and an imported library. Its entry guard must decide whether to run the CLI without breaking callers that only want its exported decision functions.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Portable Verification Boundaries
records.articleSummary: Cross-platform verification needs stable serialized contracts without rewriting the host's real filesystem paths. Context-pack labels normalize path separators to forward slashes, while paths used for I/O retain native handling. Spec generated-region comparison normalizes CRLF to LF, so an equivalent checkout does not become stale solely because of line-ending style.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Adoption When Git Writes Are Unavailable
records.articleSummary: A host can allow ordinary document edits while refusing branch, stash or commit writes in Git metadata. Adoption must distinguish that capability limit from a safe, completed migration.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00A: Blueprint, Active ADRs And The Context Map
records.articleSummary: The Blueprint describes the desired finished product. Accepted active ADR decisions carry architectural Canon; their rationale and historical alternatives remain evidence. The Lexicon routes questions to owners through its Context Map. A Spec describes a bounded destination derived from that direction and verified Actuality.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00B: Workbench Template Reformation
records.articleSummary: The reference room was changed from a fictional Example application into a copyable Workbench Template. A reference installation has its own controls, identity, local differences and installed-runtime provenance. Updating it requires preserving those facts rather than replacing the room with upstream generic files.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00C: Project Evidence And Blueprint Grilling Preparation
records.articleSummary: The project-evidence preparation seam turns explicitly named project sources into a bounded provisional JSON grilling note. It retains source identities and uncertainty, then presents owner questions without answering them.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00D: Genesis From Blueprint And ADR Decisions
records.articleSummary: The public derivation seam creates a new Workbench from a clean Template, a source project, a prepared grilling note and an explicit `genesis-plan-1` plan. It requires an absent destination and derives exactly one first capability from selected locked questions and active ADRs.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00E: Fresh Template Project Proof
records.articleSummary: A clean Template copy was used to create an independent Puffer Pond room through evidence preparation and decision-based Genesis. The demonstration then exercised a useful project Task and saved-note continuation in a fresh agent context.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00F: The Named Template Upgrade Release Gate
records.articleSummary: The producer must exercise each new Workbench version in the named Workbench_Template installation before declaring release readiness. Generic generation tests alone cannot prove an installed upgrade preserves room-owned state.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-00L: Lexicon Freshness Repair
records.articleSummary: A terminology router also contains claims that can go stale: release lineage, a current candidate version, source boundaries and its verification stamp. S-00L repaired those claims without changing the meaning of the affected definitions.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Canonical Evaluator Invocation
records.articleSummary: A successful process exit is not enough if a directly invoked evaluator never runs. A checkout reached through a path alias can make the command-line script path differ textually from its module URL even though both identify the same file.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Reproducible Adoption Provenance
records.articleSummary: Adoption proof must survive the original checkout and conversation. A cold reviewer needs the published source identity and executable reconstruction steps, not a statement that a local run once passed.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Verified Automation Run Outcomes
records.articleSummary: Run accounting distinguishes useful work, genuine absence of work and an interrupted attempt. The helper accepts exactly six categories: `actionable`, `worked`, `idle`, `owner_gate`, `collision` and `infrastructure_error`. It requires a nonempty reason and a nonnegative integer previous idle count. Unknown categories fail visibly.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Operable Genesis Readiness
records.articleSummary: A scaffold is not ready merely because expected filenames exist. Genesis readiness must establish that a cold agent can follow the declared support layout, read filled controls and select executable work.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Bounded Team Coordination (S-020)
records.articleSummary: A small agent team can work concurrently when its assignments have disjoint edit paths. A coordinator partitions the assigned work, names each lane's output and verification, receives proof, and consolidates shared state once. The useful unit of independence is the file and dependency boundary: separate worktrees preserve checkouts, but do not make competing edits to the same runtime or control independent.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Portable Workbench Architecture (S-021)
records.articleSummary: A Workbench is a filled project with root controls and a manifest-routed support area. Genesis creates a project, Adoption reconciles an existing project, and explicit upgrades carry managed components forward. LLM Workbench is the source product; ordinary operation does not depend on Foundry or a private machine's topology.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Manifest And Managed Runtime (S-023)
records.articleSummary: Schema 2 declares six support lanes—docs, specs, wiki, sessions, feedback and tools—and the machine-used collections inside them. Consumers resolve these bindings through workbench-paths. An application's root tools directory does not become harness-owned merely because the Workbench has a managed tools lane.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Governance Claims And Diagnostics (S-024)
records.articleSummary: Governance planes classify the role a claim plays in an operation. Intent, Canon, Grounding, Enduring Context, Actuality and Projection do not label entire files as authorities. A Spec can contain accepted requirements, observed results and derived views without making those claims interchangeable.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Portable Wiki Knowledge (S-025)
records.articleSummary: The Wiki holds durable explanations with explicit source links. MEMORY.md is its one router; SCHEMA.md and lane guidance define shape, maintenance and handling. Lexicon directs readers to the Wiki when they need a concept explained, and to work owners when they need current assignment or acceptance state.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Workflow Composition And Cold Continuation (S-026)
records.articleSummary: A composed workflow carries planning into implementation without depending on the original chat. Controls, the assigned Spec and Tasks, linked knowledge, named verification and a recoverable Git commit provide the continuation route. Skills resolve support paths through the manifest rather than importing private directory assumptions.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Assigned Work, Portable Stances And Delivery Boundaries
records.articleSummary: The normal entry route is `AGENTS.md -> RUNBOOK.md -> LEXICON.md`, followed by the assigned capability and only its relevant context. The Blueprint is loaded for architecture and product direction. An agent investigates missing information inside its assignment and does not invent a new queue item merely because it reaches a gap.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Feedback And Migration Integrity
records.articleSummary: Integrity checks must exercise the paths that consume a declaration rather than ban every occurrence of a legacy-looking string. S-028 rejected a blanket lane-literal linter because migration input, fixtures and explanatory text can legitimately name older locations.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Declared Integration And Recoverable Completion
records.articleSummary: A review boundary needs a real merge destination. The manifest declares `git.defaultBranch` and `git.integrationBranch` by exact name; controls and runtime resolve that declaration rather than assuming every room uses the same spelling. Exact ref enumeration avoids accepting `Integration` as `integration` merely because a filesystem is case-insensitive. `HEAD` is not a valid declared branch name.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Mechanical Permission Scope And Declared Lanes
records.articleSummary: The permission file and prose edit scope must describe the same effective boundary. A room can otherwise pass document checks while its host asks on every record write or denies a declared authorship lane.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Installed Skill Identity And Inspection
records.articleSummary: A canonical skill source and an installed copy can diverge. A review must name the path and commit it actually read; text from a user discovery root cannot be attributed to the release merely because the skill name matches.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Upgrade Layout Without Replacing Skills
records.articleSummary: An already-adopted legacy room needs an upgrade route even when replacing its installed skills is not authorized or possible. `upgrade --layout-only` performs the legacy support-root transition with presence-only skill readiness. It does not compare, mark, install, back up or replace skills. The recovery record names lifecycle upgrade, presence-only handling and an empty skill backup list. Explicit skill replacement remains a distinct, mutually exclusive mode.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Wiki Routing, Version Stamps And Safe Source Reads
records.articleSummary: A Wiki router is useful only if ordinary entry can reach it. The `room-brain-unrouted` diagnostic checks that the agent contract references the Wiki lane and the public README references MEMORY. It names the missing control route. This is a presence check, not semantic proof that every link leads to useful knowledge.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Control Fidelity Without Forced Uniformity
records.articleSummary: A room may deliberately diverge from its template. Fidelity reporting makes that divergence inspectable instead of treating every local rule as a defect or silently accepting lost qualifiers.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Release Candidate Proof And Historical Disposition
records.articleSummary: A release candidate joins capability delivery, version identity and an account of the feedback it addressed. S-035 coordinated the v3.1.2 candidate after the prerequisite capabilities were complete, measured guardrails without changing criteria, obtained exact-candidate review and proved integration containment. Its recorded PR, commit and score are historical release evidence, not the current Workbench version or a new readiness claim.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Evidence-Bounded Upgrade Claims (S-036)
records.articleSummary: Upgrade reports must distinguish what a check observes from what an operator might infer. S-036 corrected an unpublished v3.1.2 candidate where permission visibility, control fidelity and source identity had been overstated. A bounded matcher that cannot interpret a restriction reports uncertainty; it does not establish that a lane is writable.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Line-Ending-Aware Records (S-037)
records.articleSummary: Portable record readers must accept ordinary LF and CRLF checkouts without requiring each adopted repository to change Git settings. ADR and Wiki parsing share parseFrontmatter, so a correction at that seam applies consistently to both. Parsing normalizes a copy; writers preserve the destination's terminator to avoid an unrelated whole-file diff.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Source-Checked Finding Disposition (S-038)
records.articleSummary: An upstream finding is evidence to investigate, not an instruction to repair. S-038 reconciled the second v3.1.1 fix list into named capabilities, corrected unsupported report premises, and preserved the release account. Its eleven items were routed to S-039 through S-044; code ownership stayed with those capabilities.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Installed Runtime Integrity (S-039)
records.articleSummary: An installed room can compare its runtime files with the hashes in its managed-tools receipt. The authoritative expected file set also matters: an empty map, omitted file or unsafe receipt key cannot be allowed to shrink verification silently. The installed workbench-layout runtime owns this check so the room does not need the product's root tools directory to inspect itself.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Skill Presence And Repair Routes (S-040)
records.articleSummary: A refusal should name the supported way forward. S-040 made presence-only installation recognize a linked destination whose resolved directory already contains the skill, and made shared-skill refusal messages point to the layout-only route where applicable. A directory already present is skipped; this does not grant permission to overwrite unmanaged user content.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Recorded Baseline Availability (S-041)
records.articleSummary: A harness-only change may encounter a target with no reproducible green application baseline for a reason the harness change cannot affect. The owner selected record-and-proceed: the owning Spec records an unavailable baseline with evidence and one of the closed reasons host-restricted, product-broken-as-found or owner-declined-on-boundary. An unknown reason is refused.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Installed State Reporting And Repair (S-042)
records.articleSummary: Seeded documents and managed runtime files have different ownership. Runtime receipts assert managed-byte identity; a room may legitimately adapt seeded guidance. A separate seed-generation record therefore reports stale seed provenance without turning every local edit into runtime tampering.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Diagnostics Ordered By Consequence (S-043)
records.articleSummary: Doctor's human-readable output groups findings by what they do: blocking, selected-slice constraints, then informational findings. Each populated group has a count. The effect leads the row's severity, so an error with blocks none is visibly distinct from a condition that prevents work.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Adoption Preflight And Legacy Classification (S-044)
records.articleSummary: Adoption preflight reports every unreconciled root control in one refusal, with each reason, a reconcile order and a template-overwrite warning. An operator can prepare a complete correction instead of discovering one missing file on each attempt. Scaffolding is not permission to replace a project's actual controls with generic templates.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: Linked Follow-Up Reconciliation (S-045)
records.articleSummary: A completed result can leave an accepted obligation that needs a new owner. S-045 collected seven bounded follow-ups from S-039 through S-044 without reopening their completed implementation records. Dependencies and owner direction became executable work rather than disappearing into historical prose.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-046: JSON Notepad Foundation
records.articleSummary: A local JSON notepad preserves consequential context while work happens: objective, findings, corrections, uncertainty and the next authorized action. Its purpose is continuation without making the owner reconstruct lost context. The notepad is provisional evidence and never grants authority.

records.title: S-047: Visible Workbench Identifiers
records.articleSummary: A visible identifier combines its artifact type prefix with a base-62 value. It is the identity a reader sees, not an additional hidden identity beside a label. Uniqueness is scoped to that type and Workbench; unrelated Workbenches may use the same visible label.

records.title: S-048: Checkpoint Retirement And Direct Promotion
records.articleSummary: Checkpoint creation was retired while existing checkpoint history and recovery references were preserved. The legacy checkpoint command is a refusal-only compatibility boundary; it does not create new copies.

records.title: S-049: Assignment Ownership And Coordination Records
records.articleSummary: The Carry skill owns an assigned Spec or Task through the endpoint already authorized: recover context, execute, verify, reconcile records and deliver to the permitted integration boundary. It cannot expand the assignment or replace an owner-only decision.
records.reviewStatus: authored; inventory checked; semantic review pending

records.title: S-051: Core Skill Ownership And Compatibility
records.articleSummary: A core installation needs an identifiable source generation and compatible manifest policy while preserving optional shared skills and project-local ownership. Source content, installed bytes, discovery and actual native invocation are separate checks.
